title: The Case of the Cube-Shaped Clues

bands.1:
You have won Inspector Fennick's badge.

"I couldn't possibly tell you that the back door is open on Tuesdays," she says. "Today is Tuesday."

Indi hands out disguises. Gold wigs. Big foam fingers that say, "MAXX IS MY HERO." You are now a Vantafam fan tour.

Mo's wig keeps sliding off.

The Cubbler leaves a trail of cubes to the back door. Gus pockets one. "For science!"

You slip inside the Rescue Ranch.

It is not a ranch. It is a film set! There is a fake log with a sign that says, "CREATURE GOES HERE." There is a bucket of onions labelled "TEARS."

"He cries with onions," Wren hisses.

Behind a curtain is a shed full of cages. Hunchlets. Squintles. Hintatoos. "Forty-seven," Tully whispers.

A guard in a gold tracksuit sits by the door. His eyes are shut.

"I couldn't possibly say he is asleep," whispers Fennick. "But he is snoring like a leaf blower."

Zed finds a script on a clipboard. It says, "Put cute Creature in log. Pretend to find it. Cry. Use onion. Say catchphrase. Put Creature back in shed."

"That's the proof!" you whisper.

Then Mo's wig falls into a cage. The Hintatoo screeches. The guard wakes up.

"Oi!" he yells. "Fans can't come back here!"

"Why did the guard bring a ladder to work?" asks Mo. "The job had high security!"

The guard groans for ages. Meanwhile, Wren opens every cage.

The Creatures fly, glide and waddle out into the bush. The Cubbler leaves one last cube on Maxx's gold doormat.

"Beautiful," says Gus.

At the jetty, Fennick tips her hat.

"One last clue," she says. "Someone on your crew knows much more about Maxx than they are telling you."

Then she is gone. Everyone looks at each other.

Wren looks at her shoes.

bands.3:
You have won Inspector Fennick's badge, so now she gives you a clue, in her own roundabout way.

"I couldn't possibly tell you that the back door of the Rescue Ranch is left unlocked on Tuesdays," she says, examining her fingernails. "Today, by the way, happens to be Tuesday."

Indi hands out her disguises: gold wigs, gold sunnies and huge foam fingers that say, "MAXX IS MY HERO." According to Indi, you are now a Vantafam fan tour.

Mo's wig keeps sliding off his head like a nervous cat. "I'm having a bad hair day," he says, "and it isn't even my hair."

The Cubbler waddles ahead, leaving a trail of cubes all the way to the back door. Gus slips one into his pocket. "For science," he explains, to nobody's satisfaction.

The back door is unlocked, just as the Inspector didn't say. You slip inside.

The Rescue Ranch isn't a ranch at all. It's a film set! There's a fake hollow log with a sign that says, "CREATURE GOES HERE." There's a rain machine for sad scenes and a fan for windy ones. There's a bucket of onions with a label that says, "TEARS."

"He cries with onions," Wren hisses, her face going red with fury.

Behind a heavy curtain is a shed packed with cages. Hunchlets, Squintles and Hintatoos stare out at you with frightened eyes. One Hintatoo has a scratch on its left wing, shaped like a lightning bolt. Tully counts quietly. "Forty-seven," she whispers.

A guard in a gold tracksuit is slumped on a chair by the door, his eyes shut and his mouth open.

"I couldn't possibly say he's asleep," murmurs Inspector Fennick. "But he is snoring like a leaf blower."

Zed finds a clipboard hanging on a hook. Clipped to it is a script. "Episode 88. Put cute Creature in log. Pretend to find it. Cry (use onion). Say catchphrase. Put Creature back in shed. Repeat on Tuesday."

"That's our proof," you whisper, and Zed tucks it inside his jacket. "Achievement unlocked," he breathes.

Then Mo's wig slides off and drops straight into a cage. The Hintatoo inside screeches like a smoke alarm. The guard jerks awake.

"Oi!" he yells. "Fans aren't allowed back here!"

Mo steps forward bravely. "Why did the guard bring a ladder to work?" he asks. "Because the job had high security!"

The guard groans. He groans for so long and so loudly that Wren has time to open every single cage behind his back.

The Creatures fly, glide and waddle out into the misty bush, free at last. On its way out, the Cubbler stops and leaves one final cube on Maxx's gold welcome mat.

"Beautiful," says Gus, wiping away a tear.

Later, on the jetty, Inspector Fennick tips her hat to you.

"One last clue, Captain, free of charge," she says. "Someone on your crew knows a great deal more about Maxx Vantablack than they're telling you."

Then she steps back into the mist and vanishes. Everyone looks at each other.

Wren looks at her shoes.
bands.4:
Now that her badge is pinned to your jacket, Inspector Fennick offers you a clue, in her own maddeningly roundabout way.

"I couldn't possibly tell you that the back door of the Rescue Ranch is left unlocked on Tuesdays," she says, examining her fingernails with great interest. "Today, by the way, is Tuesday."

Indi hands out shiny gold wigs, gold sunnies and enormous foam fingers that say "MAXX IS MY HERO". According to Indi, you are now an official Vantafam fan tour, and nobody looks twice at a fan tour.

Mo's wig keeps sliding off his head like a nervous cat. "I'm having a bad hair day," he says, "and it isn't even my hair."

The Cubbler waddles ahead through the ferns, leaving a neat trail of cubes all the way to the back door. Gus pockets one. "For science," he explains, to nobody's satisfaction.

The back door is unlocked, exactly as the Inspector didn't say, and the Rescue Ranch, once you are inside it, turns out not to be a ranch at all. It is a film set. There is a fake hollow log with a cross of tape on the floor and a sign reading "CREATURE GOES HERE". There is a rain machine for sad scenes, a giant fan for windy ones and a spotlight labelled "HERO GLOW". Beside the camera sits a bucket of onions, labelled, in Maxx's handwriting, "TEARS".

Wren picks up an onion and turns it over in her hand. She puts it down very carefully, the way you would put down something that might explode. "He uses them to cry," she says, so quietly that only you hear. "Every single time."

Behind a velvet curtain is a shed stacked to the roof with cages. Hunchlets, Squintles and Hintatoos stare out with wide, frightened eyes, and one Hintatoo has a scratch on its left wing shaped exactly like a lightning bolt. Tully counts under her breath, the way she counts footy goals, and stops at forty-seven.

By the door, a guard in a gold tracksuit is slumped on a plastic chair, eyes shut, mouth open.

"I couldn't possibly say he's asleep," murmurs the Inspector. "But he is snoring like a leaf blower with a head cold."

On a hook beside him hangs a clipboard. Zed lifts it down. Clipped to it, in loopy gold handwriting, is a script: "Episode 88. Put cute Creature in log. Pretend to find it. Cry (use onion). Say catchphrase. Put Creature back in shed. Repeat on Tuesday."

Episode 88. Every Tuesday. You do the sum, and so, from the look on her face, does Tully.

"That's our proof," you whisper. Zed slides it inside his jacket. "Rare item acquired," he breathes.

Then, at the worst possible moment, Mo's wig slides off and drops straight into a cage. The Hintatoo inside screeches like a smoke alarm that has seen a ghost, and the guard jerks awake so suddenly that he falls off his chair.

"Oi! Fans aren't allowed back here!"

Mo steps forward, as bravely as only someone with a terrible joke can. "Why did the guard bring a ladder to work?" he asks. "Because the job had high security."

The guard groans. He groans for so long, and so loudly, clutching his head as if it hurts, that Wren has time to open every cage behind his back. When he finally looks up and demands to know who let the Creatures go, Owlibi blinks at him from the rafters, having, of course, been somewhere else the whole time.

The Creatures fly, glide and waddle out into the misty bush. On its way past, the Cubbler pauses, considers its options, and leaves one final cube in the exact centre of Maxx's gold welcome mat.

"Beautiful," whispers Gus.

Later, on the rickety jetty, the Inspector tips her hat to you.

"One last clue, Captain, free of charge," she says. "I couldn't possibly say who. But notice who knew it happens every single time."

She steps back into the mist and is gone, as if she had never been there at all.

Behind you, the crew is loading cages onto the Soggy Biscuit, arguing cheerfully about whose turn it is to sit next to Mo. Only one of them is not arguing. Wren is coiling a rope that is already coiled, and she does not look up.
